operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 11541, signed July 1, 1970 (35 FR 10737, Federal Register of July 2, 1970). Its section 2(b) provides, in the held text, that "The organizations listed herein are terminated" and lists the Council for Urban Affairs established by this order, naming it by its Executive order number and date; its section 3 provides that "This order shall be effective July 1,1970." The termination of the Council is whole-body, not partial, and the functions heretofore assigned to the listed organizations are to be performed by the Domestic Council; the first end of every clause below is therefore July 1, 1970. This clause is section 2(3), directing the Council to encourage cooperation among Federal, State and city governments. It ended with the Council on the same date: it has no application once the Council it creates, staffs or constrains no longer exists, and no held source shows it continuing independently. Executive Order 12553 later revoked the whole order by number (a later event recorded on this clause, after the first end and not the end); the amendment by Executive Order 11500 changed only section 1(c) and is recorded on that clause.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 11541, signed July 1, 1970 (35 FR 10737, Federal Register of July 2, 1970). Its section 2(b) provides, in the held text, that "The organizations listed herein are terminated" and lists the Council for Urban Affairs established by this order, naming it by its Executive order number and date; its section 3 provides that "This order shall be effective July 1,1970." The termination of the Council is whole-body, not partial, and the functions heretofore assigned to the listed organizations are to be performed by the Domestic Council; the first end of every clause below is therefore July 1, 1970. This clause is section 2(4), directing the Council to ensure that urban-affairs policies extend to the relations of urban, suburban and rural areas. It ended with the Council on the same date: it has no application once the Council it creates, staffs or constrains no longer exists, and no held source shows it continuing independently. Executive Order 12553 later revoked the whole order by number (a later event recorded on this clause, after the first end and not the end); the amendment by Executive Order 11500 changed only section 1(c) and is recorded on that clause.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 11541, signed July 1, 1970 (35 FR 10737, Federal Register of July 2, 1970). Its section 2(b) provides, in the held text, that "The organizations listed herein are terminated" and lists the Council for Urban Affairs established by this order, naming it by its Executive order number and date; its section 3 provides that "This order shall be effective July 1,1970." The termination of the Council is whole-body, not partial, and the functions heretofore assigned to the listed organizations are to be performed by the Domestic Council; the first end of every clause below is therefore July 1, 1970. This clause is section 2(5), directing the Council to seek improvement in the delivery of public services to citizens. It ended with the Council on the same date: it has no application once the Council it creates, staffs or constrains no longer exists, and no held source shows it continuing independently. Executive Order 12553 later revoked the whole order by number (a later event recorded on this clause, after the first end and not the end); the amendment by Executive Order 11500 changed only section 1(c) and is recorded on that clause.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 11541, signed July 1, 1970 (35 FR 10737, Federal Register of July 2, 1970). Its section 2(b) provides, in the held text, that "The organizations listed herein are terminated" and lists the Council for Urban Affairs established by this order, naming it by its Executive order number and date; its section 3 provides that "This order shall be effective July 1,1970." The termination of the Council is whole-body, not partial, and the functions heretofore assigned to the listed organizations are to be performed by the Domestic Council; the first end of every clause below is therefore July 1, 1970. This clause is section 2(6), directing the Council to foster decentralization of government. It ended with the Council on the same date: it has no application once the Council it creates, staffs or constrains no longer exists, and no held source shows it continuing independently. Executive Order 12553 later revoked the whole order by number (a later event recorded on this clause, after the first end and not the end); the amendment by Executive Order 11500 changed only section 1(c) and is recorded on that clause.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 11541, signed July 1, 1970 (35 FR 10737, Federal Register of July 2, 1970). Its section 2(b) provides, in the held text, that "The organizations listed herein are terminated" and lists the Council for Urban Affairs established by this order, naming it by its Executive order number and date; its section 3 provides that "This order shall be effective July 1,1970." The termination of the Council is whole-body, not partial, and the functions heretofore assigned to the listed organizations are to be performed by the Domestic Council; the first end of every clause below is therefore July 1, 1970. This clause is section 2(7), directing the Council to encourage the role of voluntary organizations in urban concerns. It ended with the Council on the same date: it has no application once the Council it creates, staffs or constrains no longer exists, and no held source shows it continuing independently. Executive Order 12553 later revoked the whole order by number (a later event recorded on this clause, after the first end and not the end); the amendment by Executive Order 11500 changed only section 1(c) and is recorded on that clause.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 11541, signed July 1, 1970 (35 FR 10737, Federal Register of July 2, 1970). Its section 2(b) provides, in the held text, that "The organizations listed herein are terminated" and lists the Council for Urban Affairs established by this order, naming it by its Executive order number and date; its section 3 provides that "This order shall be effective July 1,1970." The termination of the Council is whole-body, not partial, and the functions heretofore assigned to the listed organizations are to be performed by the Domestic Council; the first end of every clause below is therefore July 1, 1970. This clause is section 2(8), directing the Council to meet with and advise the President in emergency situations or conditions threatening civil order or civil rights. It ended with the Council on the same date: it has no application once the Council it creates, staffs or constrains no longer exists, and no held source shows it continuing independently. Executive Order 12553 later revoked the whole order by number (a later event recorded on this clause, after the first end and not the end); the amendment by Executive Order 11500 changed only section 1(c) and is recorded on that clause.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 11541, signed July 1, 1970 (35 FR 10737, Federal Register of July 2, 1970). Its section 2(b) provides, in the held text, that "The organizations listed herein are terminated" and lists the Council for Urban Affairs established by this order, naming it by its Executive order number and date; its section 3 provides that "This order shall be effective July 1,1970." The termination of the Council is whole-body, not partial, and the functions heretofore assigned to the listed organizations are to be performed by the Domestic Council; the first end of every clause below is therefore July 1, 1970. This clause is section 3(a), providing for an Executive Secretary of the Council designated by the President. It ended with the Council on the same date: it has no application once the Council it creates, staffs or constrains no longer exists, and no held source shows it continuing independently. Executive Order 12553 later revoked the whole order by number (a later event recorded on this clause, after the first end and not the end); the amendment by Executive Order 11500 changed only section 1(c) and is recorded on that clause.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 11541, signed July 1, 1970 (35 FR 10737, Federal Register of July 2, 1970). Its section 2(b) provides, in the held text, that "The organizations listed herein are terminated" and lists the Council for Urban Affairs established by this order, naming it by its Executive order number and date; its section 3 provides that "This order shall be effective July 1,1970." The termination of the Council is whole-body, not partial, and the functions heretofore assigned to the listed organizations are to be performed by the Domestic Council; the first end of every clause below is therefore July 1, 1970. This clause is section 3(b), under which the White House Office provides staff services for the Council and each represented department and agency furnishes information and assistance. It ended with the Council on the same date: it has no application once the Council it creates, staffs or constrains no longer exists, and no held source shows it continuing independently. Executive Order 12553 later revoked the whole order by number (a later event recorded on this clause, after the first end and not the end); the amendment by Executive Order 11500 changed only section 1(c) and is recorded on that clause.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 11541, signed July 1, 1970 (35 FR 10737, Federal Register of July 2, 1970). Its section 2(b) provides, in the held text, that "The organizations listed herein are terminated" and lists the Council for Urban Affairs established by this order, naming it by its Executive order number and date; its section 3 provides that "This order shall be effective July 1,1970." The termination of the Council is whole-body, not partial, and the functions heretofore assigned to the listed organizations are to be performed by the Domestic Council; the first end of every clause below is therefore July 1, 1970. This clause is section 4, a construction clause providing that nothing in the order subjects any agency or head, or any function vested by law, to the authority of another agency or head. It ended with the Council on the same date: it has no application once the Council it creates, staffs or constrains no longer exists, and no held source shows it continuing independently. Executive Order 12553 later revoked the whole order by number (a later event recorded on this clause, after the first end and not the end); the amendment by Executive Order 11500 changed only section 1(c) and is recorded on that clause.

Title 3— THE PRESIDENT
Executive Order 11452
ESTABLISHING THE COUNCIL FOR URBAN AFFAIRS
By virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and  
statutes of the United States, and as President of the United States,  
it is ordered as follows :
' S e c t i o n 1. Establishment of the Council,  (a) There is hereby estab­
lished the Council for Urban Affairs (hereinafter referred to as “the  
Council”) .
(b)  The President of the United States shall preside over meetings  
of the Council. The Vice President shall preside in the absence of the  
President.
(c) The Council shall be composed of the following:
The Vice President of the United States
The Attorney General  
Secretary of Agriculture  
Secretary of Commerce  
Secretary of Labor
Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare  
Secretary of Housing and Urban Development  
Secretary of Transportation
and such other heads of departments and agencies as the President  
may from time to time direct.
Sec. 2. Functions of the Council.  The Council shall advise and assist  
the President with respect to urban affairs and shall perform such  
other duties as the President may from time to time prescribe. In  
addition to such duties, the Council is directed to :
(1) Assist the President in the development of a national urban  
policy, having regard both to immediate and to long-range concerns,  
and to priorities among them.
(2) Promote the coordination of Federal programs in urban areas.
(3) Encourage the fullest cooperation between Federal, State, and  
city governments, with special concern for the maintenance of local  
initiative and local decision making.
(4) Ensure that policies concerning urban affairs shall extend to  
the relations of urban, suburban, and rural areas, to programs affect­
ing them, and to the movement of population between them ..
(5) Seek constant improvement in the actual delivery of public  
services to citizens.
(6) Foster the decentralization of government with the object that  
program responsibilities will be vested to the greatest possible extent  
m state and local government.
FEDERAL REGISTER, VOL. 34, NO. 17— SATURDAY, JANUARY 25, 1969

(7) Encourage the most effective role possible for voluntary or­
ganizations in dealing with urban concerns.
( 8 ) Meet with and advise the President on the occasion of emergency  
situations, or conditions threatening the maintenance of civil order or  
civil rights. N
Sec. 3. Administrative Arrangements,  (a) A  person designated by  
the President shall serve as Executive Secretary of the Council. The  
Executive Secretary shall perform such duties as the President may  
from time to time direct.
(b) In compliance with provisions of applicable law, and as neces­
sary to effectuate the purposes of this order, (1) the White House  
Office shall provide or arrange for supporting clerical administrative  
and other staff services for the Council, and (2) each Federal depart­
ment and agency which is represented on the Council shall furnish  
the Council such information and other assistance as may be available.

subjecting any department, establishment, or other instrumentality of

such agency or head, to the authority of any other such agency or head  
or as abrogating, modifying, or restricting any such function in any  
manner.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (34 FR 1223, the issue of January 25, 1969) is Executive Order 11452, Establishing the Council for Urban Affairs, dated January 23, 1969. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: Executive Order 11541 section 2(b), effective July 1, 1970 under its section 3, which terminates the Council for Urban Affairs by naming this order; this is an earlier end than the provisional status's express revocation by Executive Order 12553 (1986-02-25), which is recorded as a later event. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code search found editorial notes (under 42 U.S.C. 3531 and 31 U.S.C. 501) that recite both the termination by Executive Order 11541 and the revocation by Executive Order 12553, which I read as leads and did not rely on for the ending.

Executive Order 11541 section 2(b) provides that the functions heretofore assigned to the terminated organizations are performed by the Domestic Council, so the functions did not continue as commands of this order.","savings_check":"Executive Order 11541 was read in full. Its only saving provision, section 1(b), covers actions of the Bureau of the Budget and its Director and does not reach the Council for Urban Affairs or this order; section 2(b) states no exception or saving for the Council. The later revocation by Executive Order 12553 came after the Council had been terminated and has no bearing on the first end.","scope_check":"Fifteen clauses are inventoried by correction, covering the title and enacting clause with section 1(a), section 1(b) and (c), the section 2 lead and its eight numbered directions, section 3(a) and (b) and section 4. I read sections 3(b) and 4 as ending with the Council because they staff and constrain the Council and have no subject without it; that reading is disclosed."}

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 11541, read in full (3,633 characters), has one saving provision, section 1(b), which keeps outstanding delegations, rules, regulations, orders, circulars, bulletins and other executive or administrative action issued or taken by or relating to the Bureau of the Budget or its Director in force, until amended or revoked, as if they related to the Office of Management and Budget. That provision is limited to Bureau of the Budget actions and does not reach the Council for Urban Affairs or this order. Section 2(b) terminates the listed organizations, including the Council for Urban Affairs, outright and provides that their functions are to be performed by the Domestic Council; it states no exception or saving for the Council or its acts. Nothing shows any command of this order continuing after July 1, 1970.

research_rationale:
EO:11704 (signed 1973-02-28; 38 FR 5619 (Federal Register of March 2, 1973)) is a single-command order. The order exempts A. Everette MacIntyre, a member of the Federal Trade Commission, from compulsory retirement for age under subsection (c) of section 8335 of title 5, United States Code, until February 28, 1974. The order recites that on February 1, 1972 the President issued Executive Order No. 11642 exempting him until February 28, 1973, and states that the public interest requires that he be further exempted. The surname is MacIntyre in both the register title and the held text; the given name is spelled Everett in the register title and Everette in the held text. Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing in jobs/fr-originals; its number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: I confirm the dossier's one clause, which carries the recitals and the sole operative sentence; the text holds no other command, condition or proviso. The exemption ends by its own terms on 1974-02-28: the order's end date is quoted from the held text as "February 28,1974", recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of that day); the exclusive reading, that it ends when February 28, 1974 begins, is the alternative a reviewer should see (owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on until-dates). No later exemption of the same person is held: a name search of every held order text finds only EO 11568, EO 11642 and this order. Whether MacIntyre left office before the stated date is in no held source and is not asserted; the stated date is the latest day the exemption could operate. Searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes (all complete, none with a coverage warning): the U.S. Code search (release point 119-121, citations of the order by number in statute text and notes; edition current through 2026-10-09) recorded 0 hits; the eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML recorded 0 hits; the Federal Register catalog disposition-note search (1937 onward) recorded 0 hits for this order. I also searched every held order text (the Cruden held-text search, 33118 readable files) for the order's number; the only held text that cites it by number is its own Federal Register printing. EO 11568 (1970) and EO 11642 (1972) predate this order and do not cite it; they are found only by the person's name. A held-text search of the person's name finds only that person's own exemption orders (EO 11568, EO 11642 and EO 11704) and unrelated matches.

research_rationale:
EO 11767 of February 19, 1974 (39 FR 6603) consists of one operative paragraph designating the Organization of African Unity as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. Section 3 of EO 13377 of April 13, 2005 (70 FR 20263, published April 18, 2005) provides: "Executive Order 11767 of February 19, 1974, is revoked." The order has no own-terms sunset, condition or report date. Searches of the held corpus for the order's number found only EO 13377, the order's own texts, and an eCFR list (8 CFR 316.20) that still names the OAU designation; none revokes, supersedes or amends it earlier. The current-law table (jobs/current-law/output/ORDERS_CURRENT_LAW.csv) records one U.S. Code mention (MENTIONS.csv row usc:c26b8d90ee04, the editorial note to 22 U.S.C. 288) that lists the Organization of African Unity designation by Executive Order No. 11767 and says it was revoked by Executive Order No. 13377, section 3, April 13, 2005 (70 F.R. 20263), which agrees with the end recorded here, and one eCFR mention (8 CFR 316.20, amended through 2026-10-14) in a list of organizations that still names the Organization of African Unity with this order's date. That regulatory list makes no designation of its own and does not purport to restore the order, so it is not a current predicate for it; it is a stale list entry disclosed as a lead. The first and only dated end is the revocation on April 13, 2005.

20263Federal Register / Vol. 70, No. 73 / Monday, April 18, 2005 / Presidential Documents 
Executive Order 13377 of April 13, 2005
Designating the African Union as a Public International Or-
ganization Entitled To Enjoy Certain Privileges, Exemptions, 
and Immunities 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, including sections 1 and 12 of the 
International Organizations Immunities Act (22 U.S.C. 288 and 288f–2), as 
amended by section 569(h) of the Foreign Operations, Export Financing, 
and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2005 (Division D of Public Law 
108–447), it is hereby ordered as follows: 
Section 1. Designation. The African Union is hereby designated as a public 
international organization entitled to enjoy the privileges, exemptions, and 
immunities provided by the International Organizations Immunities Act. 
Sec. 2. Non-Abridgement. The designation in section 1 of this order is 
not intended to abridge in any respect privileges, exemptions, or immunities 
that the African Union otherwise may have acquired or may acquire by 
law. 
Sec. 3. Revocation. Executive Order 11767 of February 19, 1974, is revoked.
W

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12187, whose subject line describes providing for the base production control level for marginal properties. Sections 1-101 to 1-103 set, for pricing regulations under the Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act of 1973 and for months commencing after December 31, 1979, the base production control level for marginal properties at 20 percent of the old crude oil produced and sold from the property in 1978 (divided by 365 and multiplied by the days in the month), define marginal properties by the crude oil pricing regulations, and let the Secretary of Energy adopt conforming regulations. Executive Order 12209 of April 16, 1980 restated the order to read as follows (before: the 20 percent level applied to months commencing after December 31, 1979; after: it applies only to the months of January, February and March 1980); under owner ruling 2026-10-21 that is a strike-and-insert rewrite, the clause continues, amended, and the substance changed. Fixed period of the restated section 1-101: Executive Order 12209, signed April 16, 1980, makes section 1-101 apply only with respect to the months of January, February and March 1980, and says it was issued to permit the conversion to new oil status of all old oil production from marginal oil wells effective April 1, 1980. That fixed period ended on March 31, 1980 (inclusive; the exclusive reading would end it when that day begins), before the restatement was signed, so the pricing rule has no application to any later month and the order was functionally spent as to that rule on March 31, 1980. The restatement itself took effect on signing, April 16, 1980 (no effective date is stated). This own-terms period is a disclosed earlier candidate end and is not adopted as the first end: the restatement leaves section 1-102 (the definition of marginal properties) and section 1-103 (the Secretary of Energy's power to adopt conforming regulations) in force without any date, the restated section 1-101 still fixes the base production control level for the covered months, and under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert rewrites the clause continues, amended, until the parent order ends, which here is the express revocation by Executive Order 12553. Whether the authority of the Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act of 1973 lapsed before 1986 is not established from held sources (the statute text is not held), and such a lapse would be an unnamed instrument and a disclosed candidate only. Executive Order 12287 of January 28, 1981 (held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12287.txt; not among this packet’s citable evidence) exempted all crude oil and refined petroleum products from the price and allocation controls adopted under that Act without naming this order; it is likewise a disclosed candidate earlier end and not an end, and it is not recorded as a later event. No earlier express end was found.

The President
Executive Order 12240 of September 26, 1980
Nuclear Safety Oversight Committee
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution of the United 
States of America, and in order to provide for the extended life of the Nuclear 
Safety Oversight Committee to the extent that funds are to be made available 
therefor, it is hereby ordered as follows:
i-101. Section 1-303 of Executive Order No. 12202 is amended by adding 
thereto the following sentence: “Beginning O ctober 1,1980, such support shall 
be provided in accordance with Section 213 of the Independent Offices 
Appropriations Act, 1945 (31 U.S.C. 696).”.
1-102. Section 1-402 of Executive Order 12202 is amended to read, “The 
Committee shall terminate on September 30,1981.”.
1-103. In Section 1-102 of Executive Order No. 12202 the words “The member­
ship of the Committee shall be composed of five persons” is amended to read, 
“The membership of the Committee shall be composed of six persons.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: This clause is the order's enacting words and sections 1-1 to 1-3: the establishment of the Nuclear Safety Oversight Committee and its membership (1-101, 1-102), its advisory, reporting and agreement-making functions (1-201 to 1-211) and its staff, support, information and compensation provisions (1-301 to 1-305). research_rationale:
EO 12202 (Nuclear Safety Oversight Committee), signed 1980-03-18. The order establishes the Nuclear Safety Oversight Committee to advise on nuclear safety progress after the Three Mile Island accident (Sections 1-101, 1-102), sets its functions (1-2) and administrative provisions (1-3) and, in Section 1-402, its termination. EO 12240 (1980) extended the sunset by one year to September 30, 1981, raised membership from five to six and added a support sentence to Section 1-303. First end: the order's own sunset as amended. Section 1-402 of the original text ended the Committee on September 30, 1980; Section 1-102 of EO 12240 (signed 1980-09-26, four days before that date) rewrote Section 1-402 to provide that the Committee "terminate on September 30,1981". The Committee therefore ended on 1981-09-30 by its own terms as amended (read inclusively, the Committee exists through that day; the exclusive reading would end it when September 30, 1981 begins, and the packet holds nothing that fixes the hour). Section 22 of EO 12379 (signed 1982-08-17) and Section 4(c) of EO 12399 (effective 1982-12-31) revoke the order later, so they are later events. Inventory corrected: the dossier's single clause (offsets 700 to 7081) stopped before section 1-4, so the held order text is covered by two clauses, the enacting words with sections 1-1 to 1-3 and section 1-4 (sections 1-401 and 1-402, which carries the sunset). Machine searches adopted after reading their coverage notes: the U.S. Code search (release point 119-121, 3 hits for this order), the eCFR search as of 2026-10-14 (3 hits) and the Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition-note search (8 hits). They are leads only; the end, the later events and the savings were decided from the held Federal Register texts named in this claim. Search of the held order texts for this order's number (the packet records a bounded number-citation search over its lookup corpus, excluding clause-draft copies): apart from the order's own copies, the matching files are EO 11022, EO 11256, EO 11829, EO 12240, EO 12379, EO 12399. The files filed under EO 11022, EO 11256 and EO 11829 matched only because they carry the same Federal Register pages as the EO 12379 revocation list; they are not separate instruments naming this order.

Federal Register /  Vol. 45, No. 131 /  Monday, July 7,1980 /  Presidential Documents 45571
Presidential Documents
Executive Order 12225 of July 3, 1980
Credit Control Revocation
By the authority vested in me as President of the United States of America by  
Sections 205 and 206 of the Credit Control Act (12 U.S.C. 1904,1905), and for  
the purpose of phasing-out in an orderly fashion the credit controls authorized  
by Executive Order No. 12201, it is hereby ordered as follows:
1-101. Section 1-101 of Executive Order No. 12201 is amended effective July  
28, 1980, to read as follows: “The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve  
System is authorized to exercise authority under the Credit Control Act (12
U.S.C. 1901 e t  s e q l) to establish uniform requirements for changes in terms in  
open-end credit accounts for consumer credit; provided however, such author­
ization is revoked as of October 31,1980.“.
1-102. The authorization granted by Section 1-102 of Executive Order No.  
12201 is revoked as of August 11,1980.
1-103. The authorizations granted by Sections 1-103 and 1-104 of Executive  
Order No. 12201 are revoked as of July 28,1980.
1-104. Section 1-105 of Executive Order No. 12201 shall be amended, effective  
July 28,1980, to read as follows: “For purposes of this Order ‘consumer crédit’  
and ‘open-end credit’ shall have such meaning as may be reasonably pre­
scribed by the regulations of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve  
System.”.
1-105. Section 1-106 of Executive Order No. 12201 is revoked.
THE WHITE HOUSE,  
J u ly  3, 1980.
IFR Doc. 80-20381  
Filed 7-3 -8 0 ; 11:42 am]  
Billing code 3195-01-M

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Provision 1-101 amends Section 1-101 of Executive Order No. 12201, effective July 28, 1980, to authorize the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System to set uniform requirements for changes in terms in open-end consumer credit accounts, with that authorization revoked as of October 31, 1980. The amendment is self-executing: it was performed when its stated effective date, July 28, 1980, arrived, so the command is exhausted by performance on 1980-07-28 (the signing date, July 3, 1980, is earlier but the order defers the amendment). The amended text of Executive Order No. 12201 and its October 31, 1980 revocation are consequences of the performed amendment, not continuing commands of this order.

Federal Register /  Vol. 45, No. 131 /  Monday, July 7,1980 /  Presidential Documents 45571
Presidential Documents
Executive Order 12225 of July 3, 1980
Credit Control Revocation
By the authority vested in me as President of the United States of America by  
Sections 205 and 206 of the Credit Control Act (12 U.S.C. 1904,1905), and for  
the purpose of phasing-out in an orderly fashion the credit controls authorized  
by Executive Order No. 12201, it is hereby ordered as follows:
1-101. Section 1-101 of Executive Order No. 12201 is amended effective July  
28, 1980, to read as follows: “The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve  
System is authorized to exercise authority under the Credit Control Act (12
U.S.C. 1901 e t  s e q l) to establish uniform requirements for changes in terms in  
open-end credit accounts for consumer credit; provided however, such author­
ization is revoked as of October 31,1980.“.
1-102. The authorization granted by Section 1-102 of Executive Order No.  
12201 is revoked as of August 11,1980.
1-103. The authorizations granted by Sections 1-103 and 1-104 of Executive  
Order No. 12201 are revoked as of July 28,1980.
1-104. Section 1-105 of Executive Order No. 12201 shall be amended, effective  
July 28,1980, to read as follows: “For purposes of this Order ‘consumer crédit’  
and ‘open-end credit’ shall have such meaning as may be reasonably pre­
scribed by the regulations of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve  
System.”.
1-105. Section 1-106 of Executive Order No. 12201 is revoked.
THE WHITE HOUSE,  
J u ly  3, 1980.

Identity confirmed against the census register (executive order of 1980-07-03, Credit Control Revocation) and the held Federal Register text at 45 FR 45571, whose text layer shows Vol. 45, No. 131, Monday, July 7, 1980. The order has five numbered provisions, each a self-executing amendment or revocation of Executive Order No. 12201 with its own stated effective date (July 28, August 11 or, for the last, no date). Each is exhausted by performance on that date; the latest is August 11, 1980. The packet's held-text number search for this order returns one match, this order's own Federal Register text, so no other held text cites it and no later instrument is shown to reach it. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: This clause is the enacting words and sections 1-101 to 1-104: the establishment of the interagency Design Liaison Council of listed agency heads or their designees, the invitation to four further agencies, the chair from the Federal Council on the Arts and the Humanities, and the invitation to other interested agencies. processes o f architecture, energy conservation, engineering, graphic design, 
industrial and product design, interior design, landscape architecture, urban 
design and city planning, and other related disciplines.
1-106. The Design Liaison Council shall encourage the exchange o f informa­
tion and research on design issues among federal agencies. The Council shall 
also recom m end those changes in agency standards and procedures which 
w ill enhance the functional and visual quality of design products and 
processes.
TH E W H ITE HOUSE

EO 12379 has no effective-date clause, so the revocation took effect on signing, 1982-08-17. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12370 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Section 1 establishes, effective July 10, 1982, a three-member board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act. The command to create the board was performed when the board was appointed, but under owner ruling 2026-10-21 the order is not treated as ended by that performance or by the report. No earlier express end was found.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12370 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Section 2 directs the board to report within 30 days from the date of its creation. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C) a report deadline is not an end: the command is functionally spent when the board reports, but the order remained on the books until this revocation. The board's report is dated August 19, 1982 (held report of Emergency Board No. 194; the time was extended from August 9 to August 19, 1982 with the President's approval on July 26, 1982), so the command was functionally spent on August 19, 1982; that date is stated here and not entered as a later event because no dossier evidence record covers the transmittal letter or the extension passage. No earlier express end was found.

Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12370 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Section 3 restates the section 10 status-quo period, from the date of creation of the board until 30 days after its report. The statutory standstill (status-quo period) is likewise a spent fact and not an end; it ran until thirty days after the report dated August 19, 1982, that is to about September 18, 1982 (a computed date, not shown in a source). No earlier express end was found.

V  | |j A  dispute exists between the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and  
certain railroads represented by the National Carriers’ Conference Committee  
of the National Railway Labor Conference designated on the list attached  
hereto and made a part hereof.
This dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the provisions of the  
Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
This dispute, in the judgment of the National Mediation Board, threatens  
substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to a degree such as to deprive a  
section of the country of essential transportation service.
NOW , THEREFORE, by the authority vested in me by. Section 10 of the  
Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it is hereby ordered as  
follows:
Section 1. E s t a b lis h m e n t  o f  th e  B o a r d . There is established effective July 10,

Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 12370 (47 FR 30047, Federal Register of July 12, 1982; govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original), headed Creating an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute Between the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Certain Railroads Represented by the National Carriers’ Conference Committee of the National Railway Labor Conference and signed July 8, 1982. It creates a board to investigate the dispute between the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and certain railroads represented by the National Carriers’ Conference Committee of the National Railway Labor Conference. Inventory: the order is a board order whose operative commands are 3 clause(s) as recorded in the dossier (sec1; sec2; sec3). The list of parties attached to the order identifies the dispute and is not a separate command. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12370 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C): the report date and the end of any statutory standstill are spent facts that do not end the order; the held report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_12370_Report_of_Presidential_Emergency_Board_No._194_created_by_EO_12370_effective_July_10__6dbdcaaa92.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) shows that the board's report and recommendations were submitted to the President by a letter of transmittal dated August 19, 1982 (the cover is also dated August 19, 1982), after the President approved on July 26, 1982 an extension of the time for the report from August 9, 1982 to August 19, 1982. The board therefore made its report on August 19, 1982, the report command was functionally spent on that date, and the thirty-day period after the report ran to about September 18, 1982 (a computed date, thirty days after the transmittal date, not a date shown in the source). These dates are stated here and not entered as later events because no dossier evidence record covers the transmittal letter or the extension passage (the dossier's records from that file quote other passages of the report). operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12376, whose subject line describes increasing membership on the Presidential Commission on Drunk Driving. The single sentence amends the second sentence of section 1 of Executive Order 12358 of April 14, 1982 so that the Commission is composed of no more than 28 members appointed by the President (an increase of two). The amendment became part of the text of the parent order; the table of Executive Order 12553 lists this order by number and subject, so the revocation reaches it expressly, and no source shows the amendment being undone earlier. Executive Order 12415 of April 5, 1983 amended only section 4(b) of the parent order (the Commission’s termination date), not the membership sentence; it is a source note and not an end. The parent Commission's own termination date is a disclosed earlier candidate and not the first end: Executive Order 12415 of April 5, 1983 (48 FR 15117) amended section 4(b) of Executive Order No. 12358, as amended, to provide that the Commission shall terminate on December 31, 1983, and no held instrument extends it, so the Commission, and with it the membership ceiling this order set, had no operation after December 31, 1983 (functionally spent on that date on the inclusive reading). That instrument does not name Executive Order 12376, so under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments it is not an end; this order remained on the books until Executive Order 12553 revoked it by number. No earlier express end was found.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12393 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). The four numbered paragraphs (1-101 to 1-104) establish, effective November 16, 1982, a three-member board under section 9A of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 159a), direct a report within 30 days after creation, restate the section 9A(c) status-quo period of 120 days after creation, and provide that the board terminates ninety days after the report. The command to create the board was performed when the board was appointed, but under owner ruling 2026-10-21 the order is not treated as ended by that performance or by the report. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C) a report deadline is not an end: the command is functionally spent when the board reports, but the order remained on the books until this revocation. The actual report date is not recorded as a later event because no report text is among this packet’s citable evidence. The statutory standstill (status-quo period) is likewise a spent fact and not an end; paragraph 1-103 measures it from the creation of the board, effective November 16, 1982, for 120 days thereafter, so by the order's own terms it ran out on March 16, 1983 (a computed date, 120 days after November 16, 1982), whatever the report date was. This clause provides that the board terminates on or after the submission of its report. The report date is not held in this packet’s citable evidence, and the clause is read as a report-relative sunset that is functionally spent on the report date and not as the end, by analogy to owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C), which that ruling applies to report-relative sunsets of other boards; this analogy is a reading disclosed for the reviewer. No earlier express end was found.

Title 3— Executive Order 12393 of November 16, 1982
The Presid en t Establishing an  E m erg en cy  B o ard  T o In vestigate a  D ispute  
B etw een  T he Long Island R ail R o ad  an d  C ertain  L ab or O rga­
nizations
A dispute exists between The Long Island Rail Road and certain labor  
organizations, designated on the list attached hereto and made a part hereof,  
representing employees of The Long Island Rail Road.
The dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the provisions of the  
Railway Labor Act, as amended (“the Act”).
The New York Metropolitan Transportation Authority, the parent body of The  
Long Island Rail Road, has requested that the President establish an emergen­
cy board pursuant to Section 9A of the Act.
Section 9A(c) of the Act provides that the President, upon request of a party,  
shall appoint an emergency board to investigate and report on the dispute.
NOW, THEREFORE, by the authority vested in me by Section 9A of the Act,  
as amended (45 U.S.C. § 159a), it is hereby ordered as follows:
1-101. Establishm ent o f Board.  There is established, effective November 16,  
1982, a board of three members to be appointed by the President to investigate  
this dispute. No member shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any  
organization of railroad employees or any carrier. The board shall perform its  
functions subject to the availability of funds.
1-102. Report. The board shall report its findings to the President with respect  
to the dispute within 30 days after the date of its creation.
1-103. M aintaining Conditions.  As provided by Section 9A(c) of the Act, as  
amended, from the date of the creation of the Emergency Board, and for 120  
days thereafter, no change, except by agreement of the parties, shall be made  
by the carrier or the employees, in the conditions out of which the dispute  
arose.
1-104. Expiration.  The Emergency Board shall terminate ninety (90) days after  
the submission of the report provided for in paragraph 1-102 of this Order.

B etw een  T he Long Island R ail R o ad  an d  C ertain  L ab or O rga­
nizations
A dispute exists between The Long Island Rail Road and certain labor  
organizations, designated on the list attached hereto and made a part hereof,  
representing employees of The Long Island Rail Road.
The dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the provisions of the  
Railway Labor Act, as amended (“the Act”).
The New York Metropolitan Transportation Authority, the parent body of The  
Long Island Rail Road, has requested that the President establish an emergen­
cy board pursuant to Section 9A of the Act.
Section 9A(c) of the Act provides that the President, upon request of a party,  
shall appoint an emergency board to investigate and report on the dispute.
NOW, THEREFORE, by the authority vested in me by Section 9A of the Act,  
as amended (45 U.S.C. § 159a), it is hereby ordered as follows:
1-101. Establishm ent o f Board.  There is established, effective November 16,  
1982, a board of three members to be appointed by the President to investigate  
this dispute. No member shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any  
organization of railroad employees or any carrier. The board shall perform its  
functions subject to the availability of funds.
1-102. Report. The board shall report its findings to the President with respect  
to the dispute within 30 days after the date of its creation.
1-103. M aintaining Conditions.  As provided by Section 9A(c) of the Act, as  
amended, from the date of the creation of the Emergency Board, and for 120  
days thereafter, no change, except by agreement of the parties, shall be made  
by the carrier or the employees, in the conditions out of which the dispute  
arose.
1-104. Expiration.  The Emergency Board shall terminate ninety (90) days after  
the submission of the report provided for in paragraph 1-102 of this Order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12397, whose subject line describes continuing the National Commission on Social Security Reform. The single sentence amends section 2(b) of Executive Order 12335, which established the National Commission on Social Security Reform, so that the Commission makes its report to the President by January 15, 1983. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C) a report deadline is not an end: the command is functionally spent when the Commission reports, but the order remained on the books until this revocation. The actual report date is not recorded as a later event because no report text is among this packet’s citable evidence. Executive Order 12402 of January 15, 1983 (the held Federal Register text has its number misread by character recognition as 12432; the date, subject, amended section and the table of EO 12553, which lists 12402 after 12398, identify it) further amended section 2(b) (before: report by January 15, 1983; after: report by January 20, 1983); under owner ruling 2026-10-21 that is a strike-and-insert amendment, the clause continues, amended, and the substance (the report date) changed. Executive Order 12534 of September 30, 1985 (held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12534.txt; not among this packet’s citable evidence) revokes the parent order 12335 but does not name this order; under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (unnamed instruments) it is a disclosed candidate earlier end for the reviewer and not an end, and it is not recorded as a later event. It moves the report date of the National Commission on Social Security Reform. Inventory: one amending sentence, confirmed against the full held text. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12397, whose subject line describes continuing the National Commission on Social Security Reform. Executive Order 12402 (1983-01-15) is a later event, not an end.  The packet’s number-citation lookup over the held order texts (33,118 readable files) found citations of this number outside its own printings only in a held Wayback capture (web.archive.org) of a Social Security Administration history page for the Report of the National Commission on Social Security Reform (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_12335_Date_the_National_Commission_on_Social_Security_Reform_EO_12335_submitted_its_report__05ec610361.txt), whose contents list Executive Orders 12397 and 12402 as modifying the reporting date and which says the Commission's report was issued in January 1983; that page recites the order and does not revoke, supersede or amend it. The current-law table also records one U.S. Code mention (42 U.S.C. 401 note, MENTIONS.csv row usc:5224e903365e), a note that lists this order as amending Executive Order No. 12335 and states no end. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12447, whose subject line describes continuing the President’s Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the Federal Government. The single sentence amends section 4(b) of Executive Order 12369, as amended, to read that the Committee (the President’s Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the Federal Government) terminates on December 31, 1983, unless sooner extended. The December 31, 1983 date never operated as an end: Executive Order 12455 of December 29, 1983 amended the same section 4(b) before that date (before: terminate on December 31, 1983; after: terminate on January 31, 1984, unless sooner extended); under owner ruling 2026-10-21 that is a strike-and-insert amendment, the clause continues, amended, and the substance (the termination date) changed. Executive Order 12534 of September 30, 1985 (held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12534.txt; not among this packet’s citable evidence) revokes the parent order 12369 but does not name this order; under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (unnamed instruments) it is a disclosed candidate earlier end for the reviewer and not an end, and it is not recorded as a later event. The parent committee's amended termination date is a disclosed earlier candidate and not the first end: as further amended by Executive Order 12455 (signed December 29, 1983; 49 FR 345) section 4(b) of Executive Order No. 12369 provides that the Committee shall terminate on January 31, 1984, unless sooner extended, no held instrument extends it, and section 3 of Executive Order 12534 (signed September 30, 1985; 50 FR 40320, October 2, 1985) revokes Executive Order No. 12369 as one of the orders that established committees that have terminated or been abolished by statute or whose work is completed. The Committee, and with it the termination date this order set, therefore had no operation after January 31, 1984 (functionally spent on that date on the inclusive reading; the recital in Executive Order 12534 does not say which of its three alternatives applies to this Committee). Neither instrument names Executive Order 12447, so under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments they are not ends; this order remained on the books until Executive Order 12553 revoked it by number. No earlier express end was found.

U.S.C. 403(a)) are adjusted, as set forth at Schedule 5 attached hereto and

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 12447 (48 FR 50055, Federal Register of October 31, 1983; govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original), headed President’s Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the Federal Government and signed October 27, 1983. It extends the life of the President’s Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the Federal Government. Inventory: one amending sentence, confirmed against the full held text. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12447, whose subject line describes continuing the President’s Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the Federal Government. Executive Order 12455 (1983-12-29) is a later event, not an end.  The packet’s number-citation lookup over the held order texts (33,118 readable files) found no held text citing this order by number other than its own printings. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches were selected after reading their coverage notes (complete; no coverage warning; the USC edition runs through 2026-10-09 and the eCFR search to 2026-10-14, which cannot matter for an order whose end is shown in 1986 or earlier).

(3) The parent committee's amended termination date is a disclosed earlier candidate and not the first end: as further amended by Executive Order 12455 (signed December 29, 1983; 49 FR 345) section 4(b) of Executive Order No. 12369 provides that the Committee shall terminate on January 31, 1984, unless sooner extended, no held instrument extends it, and section 3 of Executive Order 12534 (signed September 30, 1985; 50 FR 40320, October 2, 1985) revokes Executive Order No. 12369 as one of the orders that established committees that have terminated or been abolished by statute or whose work is completed. The Committee, and with it the termination date this order set, therefore had no operation after January 31, 1984 (functionally spent on that date on the inclusive reading; the recital in Executive Order 12534 does not say which of its three alternatives applies to this Committee). operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12480 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Section 1 establishes, effective June 20, 1984, a three-member board under section 9A of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 159a), subject to the availability of funds. The command to create the board was performed when the board was appointed, but under owner ruling 2026-10-21 the order is not treated as ended by that performance or by the report. No earlier express end was found.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12480 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Section 2 directs the board to report within 30 days after the date of its creation. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C) a report deadline is not an end: the command is functionally spent when the board reports, but the order remained on the books until this revocation. The actual report date is not recorded as a later event because no report text is among this packet’s citable evidence. No earlier express end was found.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12480 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Section 3 restates the section 9A(c) status-quo period of 120 days from creation of the board. The statutory standstill (status-quo period) is likewise a spent fact and not an end. It runs from the date of the creation of the board, which section 1 fixes as effective June 20, 1984, and for 120 days thereafter, so by the order's own terms it ran out on 1984-10-18 (120 days after June 20, 1984, counted inclusive of the last day); it does not depend on the report date. No earlier express end was found.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12480 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Section 4 provides that the board terminates upon submission of the report under section 2. This clause provides that the board terminates on or after the submission of its report. The report date is not held in this packet’s citable evidence, and the clause is read as a report-relative sunset that is functionally spent on the report date and not as the end, by analogy to owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C), which that ruling applies to report-relative sunsets of other boards; this analogy is a reading disclosed for the reviewer. No earlier express end was found.

Presidential Documents
Executive Order 12480 of June 20, 1984
Establishing an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute 
Between The Long Island Rail Road and the Brotherhood of  
Locomotive Engineers
A dispute exists between The Long Island Rail Road and the Brotherhood of  
Locomotive Engineers representing employees of The Long Island Rail Road.
The dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the provisions of the  
Railway Labor Act, as amended (“the Act”).
A party empowered by the Act has requested that the President establish an  
emergency board pursuant to Section 9A of the Act.
Section 9A(c) of the Act provides that the President, upon such a request, shall  
appoint an emergency board to investigate and report on the dispute.
NOW, THEREFORE, by the authority vested in me by Section 9A of the Act,  
as amended (45 U.S.C. 159a), it is hereby ordered as follows:
Section 1 . E stablish m en t o f  B oard. There is established, effective June 20,  
1984, a board of three members to be appointed by the President to investigate  
this dispute. No member shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any  
organization of railroad employees or any carrier. The board shall perform its  
functions subject to the availability of funds.
Sec. 2. R eport. The board shall report its findings to the President with respect  
to the dispute within 30 days after the date of its creation.
Sec. 3. M aintaining C onditions. As provided by Section 9A(c) of the Act, as  
amended, from the date of the creation of the board, and for 120 days  
thereafter, no change, except by agreement of the parties, shall be made by  
the carrier or the employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose.
Sec. 4. E xpiration . The board shall terminate upon the submission of the  
report provided for in Section 2 of this Order.
THE WHITE HOUSE, 
J u n e  20, 1984.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12481 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Section 1 establishes, effective June 20, 1984, a three-member board under section 9A of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 159a), subject to the availability of funds. The command to create the board was performed when the board was appointed, but under owner ruling 2026-10-21 the order is not treated as ended by that performance or by the report. No earlier express end was found.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12481 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Section 2 directs the board to report within 30 days after the date of its creation. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C) a report deadline is not an end: the command is functionally spent when the board reports, but the order remained on the books until this revocation. The actual report date is not recorded as a later event because no report text is among this packet’s citable evidence. No earlier express end was found.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12481 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Section 3 restates the section 9A(c) status-quo period of 120 days from creation of the board. The statutory standstill (status-quo period) is likewise a spent fact and not an end. It runs from the date of the creation of the board, which section 1 fixes as effective June 20, 1984, and for 120 days thereafter, so by the order's own terms it ran out on 1984-10-18 (120 days after June 20, 1984, counted inclusive of the last day); it does not depend on the report date. No earlier express end was found.

Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12481 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Section 4 provides that the board terminates upon submission of the report under section 2. This clause provides that the board terminates on or after the submission of its report. The report date is not held in this packet’s citable evidence, and the clause is read as a report-relative sunset that is functionally spent on the report date and not as the end, by analogy to owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C), which that ruling applies to report-relative sunsets of other boards; this analogy is a reading disclosed for the reviewer. No earlier express end was found.

Establishing an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute  
Between The Long Island Rail Road and the Brotherhood of  
Railway, Airline and Steamship Clerks, Freight Handlers,  
Express and Station Employes
A dispute exists between The Long Island Rail Road and the Brotherhood of  
Railway, Airline and Steamship Clerks, Freight Handlers, Express and Station  
Employes, representing employees of The Long Island Rail Road.
The dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the provisions of the  
Railway Labor Act, as amended (“the Act”).
A party empowered by the Act has requested that the President establish an  
emergency board pursuant to Section 9A of the Act.
Section 9A(c) of the Act provides that the President, upon such a request, shall  
appoint an emergency board to investigate and report on the dispute.
NOW, THEREFORE, by the authority vested in me by Section 9A of the Act,  
as amended (45 U.S.C. 159a), it is hereby ordered as follows:
Section 1 . E stablish m en t o f  Bohrd. There is established, effective June 20,  
1984, a board of three members to be appointed by the President to investigate  
this dispute. No member shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any  
organization of railroad employees or any carrier. The board shall perform its  
functions subject to the availability of funds.
Sec. 2. R ep o rt The board shall report its findings to the President with respect  
to the dispute within 30 days after the date of its creation.
Sec. 3. M aintaining C onditions. A s provided by Section 9A(c) of the Act, as  
amended, from the date of the creation of the board, and for 120 days  
thereafter, no change, except by agreement of the parties, shall be made by  
the carrier or the employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose.
Sec. 4. E xpiration. The board shall terminate upon the submission of the  
report provided for in Section 2 of this Order.

Classification

Public Law 98-92 amends Pub. L. 96-8, 
extending the Temporary Emergency 
Food Assistance Act of 1983 through

prohibition of certain charges imposed 
by distributing agencies for the storage 
and transportation of commodities. The 
regulation, with minor changes, merely

merely quotes the language of various

reference of the user, these changes are 
also nondiscretionary. Accordingly, 
Robert E. Leard has determined that this 
is an interpretive rule and that pursuant 
to 5 U.S.C. 553 (b) and (d) this rule is 
issued without solicitation of comments 
and is made effective upon publication. 
It is the Department’s position, however, 
that the statutory prohibition against 
charges continued to be in effect prior to 
the publication of this rule. Section 
250.6(j) is being amended to avoid 
confusion regarding this matter. Section 
250.6(j) of the current regulations 
prohibits States from charging recipient

Years 1984 and 1985 which was 
published on December 16,1983 (48 FR 
55498), does not contain an extension of 
the prohibition against recipient 
agencies being assessed charges for the
storage and transportation of 
commodities.

new recordkeeping or information 
collection requirements which are 
subject to approval by the Office of

Executive Order 12554 of February 28, 1986
Nuclear Cooperation With EURATOM
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and statutes of  
the United States of America, including Section 162a(2) of the Atomic Energy  
Act of 1954, as amended (42 U.S.C. 2155(a)(2)), and having determined that,  
upon the expiration of the period specified in the first proviso to Section  
126a(2) of such Act and extended by Executive Orders No. 12193,12295,12351,  
12409, 12463, and 12506, failure to continue peaceful nuclear cooperation with  
the European Atomic Energy Community would be seriously prejudicial to the  
achievement of the United States non-proliferation objectives and would  
otherwise jeopardize the common defense and security of the United States,  
and having notified the Congress of this determination, I hereby extend the  
duration of that period to March 10,1987.
THE WHITE HOUSE,  
F e b r u a r y  28, 1986.
[FR Doc. 86-4791 
Filed 2-28-83; 3:59 pm] 
Billing code 3195-01-M

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The order is a single determination and extension: having determined that failure to continue peaceful nuclear cooperation with the European Atomic Energy Community would be seriously prejudicial to United States non-proliferation objectives, the President extends the duration of the period specified in the first proviso to Section 126a(2) of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 to March 10, 1987. The extension therefore runs by its own terms to March 10, 1987, recorded inclusive (the period runs through that day; the exclusive reading ends it when March 10 begins). Executive Order No. 12587, signed March 9, 1987 before that date, extended the period to March 10, 1988 without revoking or superseding this order; that and the later annual extension orders (Executive Orders 12629, 12670, 12706, 12753, 12791, 12840 and 12903, whose texts are held) are later events, each of which recites this order in a list of earlier extensions. Executive Orders 12629, 12706, 12753, 12791, 12840 and 12903 each state that the immediately preceding extension order shall be superseded on the effective date of the new order (12629 supersedes 12587, 12706 supersedes 12670, 12753 supersedes 12706, 12791 supersedes 12753, 12840 supersedes 12791 and 12903 supersedes 12840); Executive Orders 12587 and 12670 contain no supersession sentence. None of them supersedes or revokes this order, so none is treated as ending it. The effective date of each later order is taken as its signing date because none states a different one.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The sole paragraph amends section 2(b) of Executive Order 12575 by striking the date February 19, 1987 and inserting February 26, 1987, extending the Board's time to submit findings and recommendations. Terminated by express revocation of the parent order. Section 3 of Executive Order 12610, signed September 30, 1987, begins "Sec. 3. The following Executive Orders, which established committees that" and ends its lead-in with "have terminated or whose work is completed, are revoked:"; item (g) reads "Executive Order No. 12575, establishing the President’s Special Review" (the line continues "Board."). Section 5 reads "Sec. 5. This Order shall be effective September 30,1987." The amended date lives in the parent's section 2(b), so it ends when the parent is revoked, 1987-09-30. Disclosed reading: the order does not name Executive Order 12584, and the amendment was itself made on signing, 1987-02-19; under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments the clause continues, amended, until the parent ends. The extended report date, February 26, 1987, is a deadline and not an end. The parent's own-terms sunset is a disclosed candidate earlier end and is not recorded as the end. Section 4 of Executive Order 12575 reads 'The Board shall terminate 30 days after submitting its report to the President.' A held Public Papers text (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_12575_Date_the_President_s_Special_Review_Board_Tower_Commission_submitted_its_report_to_th_1875c02b67.txt, PPP-1987-book1 PDF pages 197-201; a held text lead from a scan's text layer, not an authenticated original) prints 'Remarks on Receiving the Final Report of the President’s Special Review Board on the National Security Council' dated February 26, 1987, so the report was received on that date, which is the date to which this order moved the report deadline, and 30 days after it is 1987-03-28. That sunset belongs to the parent's Board and is keyed to a report; under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), applied here by disclosed analogy to a report-relative sunset, it is a spent fact and not an end of the order, which stays on the books until express revocation. No held source states that the Board was terminated on a date, apart from section 4 of the parent itself. Executive Order 12581 of January 28, 1987 (52 FR 2979) amended section 2(b) of Executive Order No. 12575 before this order and is an earlier amendment, not a later event; this order then deletes the date it set (February 19, 1987).

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register machine text of Executive Order 12584 (52 FR 5429, PDF page 11 of the 1987-02-23 issue; sha256 9ce8d3b6...), headed "President’s Special Review Board" in the OCR layer, which splits many words with stray spaces. It is signed February 19, 1987, which matches the census register row (1987-02-19, President's Special Review Board). The machine heading search did not resolve the heading; I confirmed it by reading the OCR heading line, which reads Executive Order 12584 of February 19, 1987. Text and inventory: one operative paragraph; it extends the time within which the Board may submit its findings and recommendations by amending section 2(b) of Executive Order 12575 (as amended), deleting the date February 19, 1987 and inserting February 26, 1987. The inventory is one clause and I confirm it. Ending: Executive Order 12610 (signed 1987-09-30, effective that day) revokes Executive Order 12575, the parent that the amendment changes; the amended provision cannot operate without its parent. The amendment itself was made when signed, and its effect (the changed report date) lives in section 2(b) of the parent until the parent ends; that is the reading of the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments, disclosed as a reading. The parent's own-terms sunset is a disclosed candidate earlier end and is not recorded as the end. Section 4 of Executive Order 12575 reads 'The Board shall terminate 30 days after submitting its report to the President.' A held Public Papers text (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_12575_Date_the_President_s_Special_Review_Board_Tower_Commission_submitted_its_report_to_th_1875c02b67.txt, PPP-1987-book1 PDF pages 197-201; a held text lead from a scan's text layer, not an authenticated original) prints 'Remarks on Receiving the Final Report of the President’s Special Review Board on the National Security Council' dated February 26, 1987, so the report was received on that date, which is the date to which this order moved the report deadline, and 30 days after it is 1987-03-28. That sunset belongs to the parent's Board and is keyed to a report; under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), applied here by disclosed analogy to a report-relative sunset, it is a spent fact and not an end of the order, which stays on the books until express revocation. No held source states that the Board was terminated on a date, apart from section 4 of the parent itself. Executive Order 12581 of January 28, 1987 (52 FR 2979) amended section 2(b) of Executive Order No. 12575 before this order and is an earlier amendment, not a later event; this order then deletes the date it set (February 19, 1987).
